objective: Implement a bounded Windows desktop shell spike that embeds the existing DR24 Workbench, runs FastAPI on a dynamically allocated loopback port, stores runtime state under per-user application data, and authenticates API requests through an in-memory session token. Keep GUI dependencies optional and preserve the scientific baseline.
previous_knowledge_consumed: The owner selected standalone Windows desktop delivery for the first Park preview.
The current server entry point binds to 127.0.0.1:8000 and has no managed desktop lifecycle.
FastAPI create_app(settings=...) supports per-instance configuration and Bearer authentication for /v1 endpoints.
The Workbench uses fetchJson as its shared API request path.
Current API storage defaults include paths relative to the working directory.
pywebview provides an embedded Windows Edge WebView2 renderer and a JavaScript/Python bridge.

baseline.status: Branch is based on the PR #307 DR24 descriptive-summary candidate. No main merge, production model, dataset, frozen feature contract, benchmark or release is changed.

expected_improvement: Managed local API startup and shutdown with a health-readiness check.
Loopback-only binding and a dynamically allocated port.
Per-user cache, job, result, settings and scientific-evidence paths.
Bearer authentication for all /v1 requests in desktop mode.
Optional Windows desktop dependencies that do not affect server-only installations.
Normal browser Workbench behaviour remains unchanged when desktop mode is absent.

reliability.before: The existing server entry point uses a fixed port and is not managed by a desktop window.
reliability.after: A testable runtime binds an ephemeral loopback socket, waits for /health and stops the Uvicorn thread.

reproducibility.before: No Windows desktop runtime or package build exists.
reproducibility.after: A Windows CI build and clean-machine validation are planned; neither is accepted by this code-only spike.

measurement.trade_off: A small pywebview shell reuses the current Workbench, but WebView2 availability, Windows packaging, native navigation controls and dependency locking remain open.

evidence: Added LocalApiServer with a pre-bound ephemeral socket, loopback restriction, /health readiness check and managed shutdown.
Added per-user settings for cache, job database, result database, app settings and scientific evidence.
Added an in-memory token bridge for the desktop Workbench.
Added desktop-only Bearer headers to fetchJson and a DOM guard against external anchor navigation.
Added a Windows desktop entry point and optional pywebview/PyInstaller extras.
Added tests for per-user data paths, token requirements, loopback binding, dynamic-port startup/shutdown and health timeout.
validation.blocker: Run exact-head CI and a Windows x64 package build. Verify the embedded navigation policy at the native WebView boundary and complete clean Windows acceptance.

root_causes: The current API entry point hard-codes port 8000 and has no desktop process lifecycle.
The browser Workbench did not authenticate API calls because browser mode did not require a token.
Some API data paths are relative to the current working directory.
unresolved: WebView2 and .NET runtime behavior are not tested on the actual Windows device.
PyInstaller may need hidden imports and explicit inclusion of static and benchmark data.
JavaScript navigation guards are not a substitute for a verified native WebView navigation boundary.
A separate fully resolved Windows dependency lock, signed installer, upgrade/uninstall flow and clean-machine acceptance are not available.
Persian UX, target-user testing and written Park evaluation terms remain open.

findings: FastAPI app factory configuration can support a dedicated per-user desktop instance.
A pre-bound loopback socket can avoid fixed port conflicts, subject to Windows runtime validation.
The same Workbench can support a desktop-only token flow without changing ordinary browser mode.
API tokens must stay in memory and must not be written to URLs, logs, settings or exported provenance.
A PyInstaller one-folder build is an engineering test, not a completed installer.

open_blockers: Pass exact-head Linux tests and Ruff checks.
Build a Windows one-folder package and verify that static Workbench and benchmark configuration assets are included.
Test missing WebView2 behavior and verify that no browser fallback occurs.
Verify that all desktop /v1 requests use the in-memory Bearer token.
Verify native navigation restrictions against external URLs and untrusted redirects.
Test startup, shutdown, port collision, health timeout, network loss and process cleanup on Windows.
Complete clean Windows 11 installation, live DR24 retrieval, JSON export, offline relaunch, upgrade and uninstall.
Create a fully resolved Windows dependency lock and retain build hash and SBOM.
Obtain written Park evaluation/demo terms before external distribution.

knowledge_carried_forward: Windows desktop shell remains an engineering spike, not a distributable application.
pywebview 6.2.1 and PyInstaller 6.22.3 are optional candidate dependencies, subject to the Windows proof-of-concept.
The API must bind only to loopback and use a dynamic port.
The desktop token remains in memory and is provided through the pywebview API bridge.
The browser Workbench continues to operate when desktop=1 is absent.
Preserve v0.2.0 and keep DR24 inference blocked.
No external installer distribution before Windows acceptance and written legal approval.
